copy.blurb:
Sunday 21 June 2026 at 19:00 UTC. Belgium and IR Iran on the card. On the IR Iran side, the engine's number sits +15.3pp clear of the market — one of the widest in the priced field this far out from kickoff.

Public Elo rates Belgium 120 points higher than the other side (Belgium 1860, IR Iran 1740). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Belgium to win at 51%, the draw at 23%, and IR Iran to win at 26%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. IR Iran on the win side reads 26%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Belgium to win at 68%, the draw at 21%, and IR Iran to win at 10%. The IR Iran side trades at 10% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +852. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 26%, +15.3pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the IR Iran side that lower bound is 21% — +10.5pp clear of the market's 10%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 31 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives IR Iran a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +15.3pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +15.3pp gap across model and market on the IR Iran side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates IR Iran at 26%; Polymarket sits at 10%.
copy.title: Belgium v IR Iran · the model leans IR Iran
